plan.planning_summary: Refining route_04 (chirped DBR dichroic filter) based on prior iteration evidence. The 20-layer version (iteration_04) achieved best_target_score=0.918, while the 16-layer monotonic constrained version (iteration_09) scored 0.666. Feedback directives specify: (1) deterministic linear chirp seed initialization to escape periodic basins, (2) increased perturbation magnitude for early generations to allow thick end-layers. Three complementary routes explore: refined 20-layer with explicit chirp seed, 24-layer for extended reflection bandwidth, and 18-layer asymmetric chirp profile. All routes maintain HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica, normal incidence, dual-band spectral separation objective.

routes.title: 20-Layer Chirped DBR with Deterministic Linear Chirp Seed
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 chirped dielectric stack initialized with explicit linear thickness gradients (odd layers: 45-90 nm ramp, even layers: 65-130 nm ramp) will achieve higher target scores than unseeded optimization by escaping local minima associated with periodic quarter-wave stacks.
routes.design_principle: Chirped Bragg reflector with linearly varying optical thickness across the stack to broaden the high-reflectance band (400-700 nm) while maintaining a transmission window at 1530-1565 nm through destructive interference cancellation in the telecom band.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2 | SiO2]_10 | Fused Silica substrate (20 finite layers total, alternating high/low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses (20 continuous variables, bounded 30-250 nm)
Initial thickness profile seeded with linear chirp
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain total layer count at exactly 20
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses within typical ion-beam sputtering capability (30-250 nm)
No thickness coupling constraints to allow optimizer full freedom
theory_basis: Chirped DBR bandwidth broadening theory: varying layer optical thickness expands reflection band beyond periodic stack limit
Prior iteration_04 achieved 0.918 target score with 20-layer chirped design
expected_advantages: Deterministic initialization reduces optimizer dependence on random seed
Linear chirp profile explicitly targets broad visible reflection band
known_risks: Chirp profile may not be optimal for asymmetric dual-band requirement
Optimizer may still converge to local minima despite seeding
Thick end-layers may introduce absorption or scattering losses not modeled
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate under normal incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (20 finite layers). Initialize thicknesses with deterministic linear chirp: odd-indexed layers (HfO2) ramp from 45 nm to 90 nm across the stack, even-indexed layers (SiO2) ramp from 65 nm to 130 nm. Optimization bounds: 30-250 nm per layer. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with increased perturbation magnitude (3x baseline) for first 3 generations. Score candidates by: (1) average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band, (2) average reflectance in 400-700 nm band, with equal weighting. Wavelength sampling: 5 nm steps in both bands. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all physically valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive for deterministic linear chirp seed initialization and increased early-generation perturbation to escape periodic basin. Maintains 20-layer count from best-performing iteration_04 (score 0.918) while adding explicit initialization protocol absent in prior runs.

routes.title: 24-Layer Extended Chirped DBR for Broader Visible Rejection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 24 in a chirped HfO2/SiO2 stack will broaden the 400-700 nm reflection band edge coverage and improve dual-band spectral separation, as additional layers provide more degrees of freedom for band-edge shaping.
routes.design_principle: Extended chirped Bragg reflector: additional layer pairs allow finer control over reflection band edges while maintaining telecom transmission window through careful thickness distribution.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2 | SiO2]_12 | Fused Silica substrate (24 finite layers total, alternating high/low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses (24 continuous variables, bounded 30-250 nm)
Linear chirp initialization profile scaled for 24 layers
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain total layer count at exactly 24
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses within typical ion-beam sputtering capability (30-250 nm)
Increased layer count may increase deposition time and stress accumulation
theory_basis: DBR reflection bandwidth scales with layer count for chirped designs
Prior iteration_04 (20 layers) outperformed iteration_09 (16 layers), suggesting layer count matters
expected_advantages: 4 additional layers provide more optimization freedom for band-edge control
May achieve sharper transition between reflection and transmission bands
known_risks: Diminishing returns beyond 20 layers may not justify added complexity
Increased layer count may reduce robustness to thickness variations
Optimizer search space expands, potentially requiring more iterations

Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2 repeated 12 times (24 finite layers total, starting with HfO2). Initialize thicknesses with deterministic linear chirp: odd-indexed layers (HfO2) ramp from 40 nm to 95 nm across the stack, even-indexed layers (SiO2) ramp from 60 nm to 135 nm. routes.revision_reason: Explores whether layer count increase from 20 to 24 improves performance beyond iteration_04's 0.918 score. Tests hypothesis that additional layers provide meaningful band-edge control for the 400-700 nm reflection requirement while maintaining 1530-1565 nm transmission.

routes.title: 18-Layer Asymmetric Chirp Profile for Band-Edge Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An asymmetric chirp profile (steeper thickness gradient at stack entrance, shallower at substrate interface) will better match the asymmetric spectral requirement (broad 400-700 nm reflection vs narrow 1530-1565 nm transmission) than symmetric linear chirp.
routes.design_principle: Asymmetric chirped DBR: front layers optimized for short-wavelength reflection (400-550 nm), rear layers optimized for long-wavelength reflection (550-700 nm), with central layers tuned for telecom transmission preservation.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2 | SiO2]_9 | Fused Silica substrate (18 finite layers total, alternating high/low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses (18 continuous variables, bounded 30-250 nm)
Piecewise linear chirp initialization: front 6 layers steep ramp, middle 6 layers plateau, rear 6 layers shallow ramp
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain total layer count at exactly 18
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses within typical ion-beam sputtering capability (30-250 nm)
Asymmetric profile may require more precise thickness control at layer interfaces
theory_basis: Asymmetric DBR designs can tailor reflection band shape for non-symmetric spectral requirements
18 layers balances optimization freedom with search space complexity
expected_advantages: Better matching of asymmetric dual-band spectral requirement
Reduced layer count vs 20/24-layer designs may improve robustness
Piecewise chirp may capture optimal thickness distribution more efficiently
known_risks: Piecewise initialization may bias optimizer away from global optimum
18 layers may be insufficient for full 400-700 nm coverage
Asymmetric profile may introduce unexpected transmission dips in telecom band

routes.revision_reason: Tests asymmetric chirp hypothesis as alternative to symmetric linear chirp in route_04_ref_01. 18-layer count chosen as intermediate between iteration_09's 16 layers (score 0.666) and iteration_04's 20 layers (score 0.918) to balance search complexity with optimization freedom.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating the 1530-1565 nm transmission priority in all routes

Prior iteration_04 (20-layer, score 0.918) vs iteration_09 (16-layer, score 0.666) evidence directly informs layer count choices: route_04_ref_01 maintains 20 layers, route_04_ref_02 tests 24 layers, route_04_ref_03 tests 18 layers
Feedback directives explicitly require deterministic linear chirp seed and increased early-generation perturbation, implemented in all three routes' execution requests
unresolved_decisions: Optimal layer count between 16-24 layers remains uncertain; routes test 18, 20, and 24 to bracket the design space
Symmetric vs asymmetric chirp profile optimality unknown; route_04_ref_01/02 use symmetric linear, route_04_ref_03 tests asymmetric piecewise
Whether increased perturbation magnitude improves convergence or introduces instability requires empirical validation across all three routes
